name: devflow
description: Rob's development workflow: an always-on working mode for plain requests, and flows you start by command (small change, feature, bug, big job) that stop once to show the plan, then build, prove and ship. Includes a git safety hook.

git_guard.title: Git safety hook
git_guard.description: Block git push, reset --hard, clean -f, branch -D, and commands that discard the whole working tree while a devflow flow is running. You run those yourself.

no_comments.title: No code comments
no_comments.description: Claude adds no comments or docstrings to code it writes or edits, including ones that explain the change, unless you ask. Existing comments stay.

mode.title: devflow mode
mode.description: How Claude works on a request you make without /devflow:start: seven rules and six steps, about 400 words loaded into every session. Off: plain requests get no devflow guidance.

adversarial_review.title: Adversarial review
adversarial_review.description: When a flow sends two fresh subagents to try to break the change. risky changes: auth, permissions, payments, data migration or deletion, concurrency, public APIs. always: every feature and big job. never: skip it.

subagent_count.title: Subagents at once
subagent_count.description: How many tickets of a big job are built at the same time, each by its own subagent. 1 to 10.

subagent_model.title: Subagent model
subagent_model.description: The model that builds a big job's tickets. auto: the fast model for tickets marked simple and the strong model for ones marked complex (Sonnet and Opus). Any model name: that model for every ticket.

tracker.title: Issue tracker
tracker.description: Where a big job's plan and tickets are published. auto: GitHub or GitLab, read from the git remote, else files in the flow's folder.
